explain.say: An estuary is the wide mouth of a river where fresh river water meets salty seawater, rising and falling with the tides. The Thames, the Hudson and the Hooghly all end in estuaries.

explain.say: Heavier salt water from the sea creeps upriver along the bottom in a wedge, pushed further in at high tide. Where the two meet and churn, the water becomes brackish, partly salty.

explain.say: Where fresh and salt water mix, fine mud clumps together and settles, building mudflats and salt marshes. They are packed with worms and shellfish, feeding wading birds and young fish.

faq.q: Why does fresh water float on salt water?
faq.a: Salt water is denser, because the dissolved salt adds mass without taking up much extra room. So fresh river water tends to spread out on top of the sea until waves and tides mix them.
asks: Do river water and sea water mix?

faq.a: Brackish water is a mix of fresh and salt water, saltier than a river but less salty than the sea. Estuaries and some coastal lagoons are brackish.

faq.q: Why are estuaries important for wildlife?
faq.a: Rivers bring nutrients and the tides bring food twice a day, so mudflats and marshes teem with worms and shellfish. They feed huge flocks of birds and are nurseries for young fish.
asks: Why do birds gather on mudflats?

faq.a: A wedge of heavier seawater that pushes upriver along the bottom of an estuary, underneath the lighter fresh water flowing out on top.
asks: How far does seawater go up a river?

faq.q: What is the difference between an estuary and a delta?
faq.a: An estuary is a funnel-shaped river mouth that the tides flood and empty. A delta forms where a river drops so much sediment that it builds new land out into the sea.
asks: Is an estuary the same as a river mouth?

facts: Seawater is about 2.5 percent denser than fresh water.
The Severn Estuary in Britain has one of the largest tidal ranges in the world, around 14 metres.

quiz.say: In an estuary, where is the saltiest water usually found?
quiz.show: In an estuary, the saltiest water is usually…
quiz.why: Seawater is denser than river water, so it creeps in underneath as a salt wedge.

wrong.1: The surface usually has the lighter, fresher river water.
wrong.2: The source is far inland where the water is completely fresh.
